# Visual Gallery {#sec-gallery}

Every kind of diagram the book draws, each with the few lines that make it. All of them come from one module, `books/shared/dsa_viz.py`, so a figure in any chapter looks like the figures in every other chapter, and every one is drawn twice, once for the light theme and once for the dark. Open a "Code" fold to copy a starting point for a new figure.

```{python}
#| include: false
import sys

sys.path[:0] = ["../shared", "../traces"]
import dsa_viz as V
```

## Arrays, pointers and regions {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-array}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    V.array(ax, p, [2, 7, 11, 15, 18, 21], regions=[(1, 4, "cyan", "window")],
            pointers=[(1, "lo", "indigo"), (3, "hi", "pink")], label="a")
V.show(draw)
```

`V.array`: cells, indices, coloured regions with a bracket, and pointers above or below.

:::

## Several rows over time {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-trace}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    V.trace(ax, p, [
        dict(values=[5, 3, 8, 1], pointers=[(0, "i", "indigo")], label="step 1"),
        dict(values=[3, 5, 8, 1], pointers=[(1, "i", "indigo")], colors={0: "green"}, label="step 2"),
        dict(values=[3, 5, 1, 8], pointers=[(2, "i", "indigo")], colors={3: "green"}, label="step 3"),
    ])
V.show(draw)
```

`V.trace`: one `array` row per step, stacked top to bottom.

:::

## Trees {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-tree}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    N = V.Node
    root = N("f(4)", [N("f(3)", [N("f(2)"), N("f(1)", color="green")]), N("f(2)", color="pink", note="repeat")])
    V.tree(ax, p, root)
V.show(draw)
```

`V.tree` with `V.Node`: recursion trees, binary trees, DFS trees. A node can carry a colour and a note.

:::

## Tables and DP grids {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-grid}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    cells = [["1", "1", "1", "1"], ["1", "2", "3", "4"], ["1", "3", "6", "10"]]
    V.grid(ax, p, cells, row_labels=["r0", "r1", "r2"], col_labels=["c0", "c1", "c2", "c3"],
           colors={(2, 3): "pink", (1, 3): "cyan", (2, 2): "cyan"})
V.show(draw)
```

`V.grid`: a 2D table. Colour the cell being filled and the cells it reads.

:::

## Three-index DP in 3D {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-iso}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    vals = {(i, j, k): str(i + j + k) for i in range(3) for j in range(4) for k in range(3)}
    cols = {(2, 3, 2): "pink", (1, 3, 2): "cyan", (2, 2, 2): "cyan", (2, 3, 1): "amber"}
    V.iso_grid(ax, p, (3, 4, 3), values=vals, colors=cols)
V.show(draw)
```

`V.iso_grid`: a table `dp[i][j][k]` as stacked isometric plates, one per `k`. The pink cell reads two cells of its own layer (cyan) and one cell of the layer below (amber), which is the shape of a three-index transition such as "two walkers" or "at most $k$ operations".

:::

## Stacks, bars and intervals {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-misc}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    V.stack(ax, p, ["(", "[", "{"], x=0, y=0, title="stack")
    V.bars(ax, p, [2, 1, 5, 6, 2, 3], x=3.5, y=0, height=3.0, colors={2: "pink", 3: "pink"})
V.show(draw)
```

`V.stack` and `V.bars`: a monotonic stack, a histogram.

:::

::: {#fig-gal-intervals}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    V.intervals(ax, p, [(1, 4, "A", "indigo"), (3, 6, "B", "pink"), (5, 8, "C", "green"), (7, 9, "D", "amber", True)])
V.show(draw)
```

`V.intervals`: one interval per row over a shared axis; the last field marks a dashed (rejected) interval.

:::

## Flows {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-flow}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    nodes = {"r": (0, 0, "Read constraints", "indigo"), "p": (4.2, 0, "Pick pattern", "cyan"),
             "c": (8.4, 0, "Code + stress", "green")}
    V.flow(ax, p, nodes, [("r", "p", ""), ("p", "c", "")], w=3.6)
V.show(draw)
```

`V.flow`: boxes and arrows for recipes and decision paths.

:::

## Animations {.unnumbered}

::: {#fig-gal-anim}

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code"
vals = [4, 2, 7, 1, 9]
best = [max(vals[: k + 1]) for k in range(len(vals))]

def frame(ax, p, k):
    V.array(ax, p, vals, pointers=[(k, "i", "indigo")], colors={vals.index(best[k]): "green"})

V.animate(frame, len(vals), captions=[f"i = {k}: best so far = {best[k]}" for k in range(len(vals))])
```

`V.animate(draw_frame, n_frames, captions=…)`: 2 to 15 frames, saved as small image files, with play, step and keyboard control (focus the figure, then ← → and space). In a PDF the last frame is printed.

:::

## Reviewing figures {.unnumbered}

`python scripts/review_figs.py` renders every figure of the chapters you name into two contact sheets, one per theme, so you can check them all at a glance before a build.
